A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSI research and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original material can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering; v2 Appendices A–B are retained within v3's expanded Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v2 reports original Llama-2 intervention experiments, comparisons with SFT and other steering methods, human–judge agreement, and direction-similarity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on other models, safety behaviors, MMLU, direction sampling, and jailbreak resistance.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the contrastive steering vector, scaled head-wise activation addition, and binary-choice head sweep. Additional models and negative-direction interventions reuse this procedure; no new algorithmic component or architectural adaptation is specified.

E1.justification: Beyond the three coordination scenarios already evaluated in v2, v3 adds corrigibility, myopic reward, and survival instinct evaluations in Appendix C, MMLU in Section 4.6, and grandmother-jailbreak inputs in Section 4.7 and Appendix F. These substantially broaden behavioral, capability, and adversarial coverage.

E2.justification: The original Llama-2 comparisons retain baseline, SFT, CAA, and ITI. v3 adds a random-head intervention comparator to the jailbreak experiment in Table 8 and additionally investigates multi-layer variants of the layer-wise baseline in Appendix E.

E3.justification: v3 adds three model configurations, a 570-question MMLU evaluation with a 1,024-token limit, and jailbreak-control protocols. The stated 180/180/50 split, with 100 validation examples used for screening, becomes 100 randomly chosen validation examples and a 50-example prior-work test set, with training size unspecified. Llama-2 CAA vectors are now described as taken from prior work rather than derived from HSI examples, and the judge range changes from 1–10 to 0–10. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of collateral capability effects on MMLU, sensitivity to direction-defining sample triplets, selected versus random heads for jailbreak defense, semantic versus superficial token-activation patterns, and single versus multiple-layer interventions. The existing cosine-similarity analysis and Appendix A–B case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5 newly reports direction sampling under three random seeds, with separate triplet results in Table 7. Table 3 also identifies the retained judge–human correlation as Pearson correlation. This does not establish increased repetitions for existing experiments, and confidence intervals or significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: The original table values and Figures 1–4 remain unchanged, including v2 Table 5 becoming v3 Table 9. Added results include Ministral HSI 7.46 versus layer-wise 3.35, MMLU accuracy 0.46 at baseline versus 0.51 and 0.29 at strengths 35 and 55, direction-sampling accuracies of 0.73–0.87, jailbreak reductions, and three additional safety-domain scores. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: The attention decomposition, contrastive-vector definition, and additive-intervention equations in Section 3.1 are unchanged. Neither version provides additional formal propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the main contribution from Llama-2 AI-coordination steering to effectiveness across models and additional safety behaviors. It also makes negative-direction prevention of a common jailbreak a headline contribution, whereas v2 only suggested possible beneficial applications.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning semantic head specialization, capability preservation at the selected strength, robustness to direction-defining examples, and server-side jailbreak defense. It discusses normalization-related applicability boundaries and larger-model sweep costs, while dropping explicit limitations concerning manual head selection and required head-level linear separability.

D1.justification: v3 adds model/checkpoint identifiers, per-domain head and intervention-strength settings in Appendix C, the MMLU generation limit, and the complete jailbreak prompt in Appendix F. Hardware, the SFT recipe, and the code/data access link remain unchanged. Settings for every additional model are not fully specified.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands discussion of closely related approaches through persona vectors, ACT, CONFST, Pinpoint Tuning, and semantics-adaptive interventions, and explicitly positions HSI's selection strategy against activation-probe accuracy. References to Qiu's spectral editing, Turner's Activation Addition, and van der Weij's broad-skills steering are removed. Publication updates to retained Arditi and Rimsky works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and subdivides related work, condenses the direction-analysis and limitations discussions, and revises the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. SFT moves into hyperparameter screening. These changes reshape the narrative beyond simply adding experiments, although much of the method exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from the JAIR template to TMLR formatting, relocates existing displays, and reformats Appendix A into separately labeled response panels. It adds Tables 5–8 and 10 and Figures 5–8. Original Figures 1–4 retain their content, and the original cosine-similarity table is merely renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's stated single-model and single-behavior limitations through additional model and domain evaluations. MMLU, direction-sampling, and random-head-controlled jailbreak experiments materially improve assessment of generality, specificity, and tradeoffs, including capability degradation at stronger interventions. Incomplete settings and uncertainty reporting, reused domain baselines, and the removed manual-selection caveat limit the gains, but the empirical support is substantially stronger overall.
